units.translation: μήτε [neither], with δέ [but] responding, Suppl. 987 ὡς ἔχοιμι τίμιον γέρας, καὶ μήτ᾽ ἀέλπτως δορικανεῖ μόρῳ θανὼν λάθοιμι, χώρᾳ δ᾽ ἄχθος ἀείζων πέλοι [that I might have an honorable prize, and neither unexpectedly by a spear-won death might I perish unnoticed, nor be a living burden to the land], with an obvious fault. There is no doubt that one part of the sentence has fallen out, which is the opinion of Paley and of Wecklein in his Aeschylean Studies p. 88.
so that neither any of the gods nor any of men rejoiced at these things.
so that neither before the proper time nor beyond the stars might the bolt be hurled in vain.
so that neither in harbor might it have the tossing of the wave nor run aground.
so that neither to flee nor to ward off death.
so that neither to save myself nor to move my step.
so that neither strife over reprisals will seize us nor will we be made subject.
that to marry in one's own rank is by far the best, and neither being among those softened by wealth nor among those puffed up by birth, to desire a marriage with a poor man.
and neither to accompany the tomb-pouring libations nor to approach with shrill lamentations.
How shall I dare neither to weep for you nor to escort you to the tomb?
These things are for me a double, unutterable care in my heart: neither to honor the abundance of unmanly wealth, nor to let the light shine for those without wealth.
Know this well: do not tell you twice, neither word nor deed.
How shall I revere you, neither exalting too high nor bending too low?
I advise to honor that which is neither anarchic nor despotic, protecting it for the citizens.
and neither any of the inhabitants nor of the newcomers to lead.
neither to rejoice nor to grieve mortals.
neither to leave the wine-jars nor the water-jars.

praise neither a life without rule nor one under a master.
do not cast bloody whetstones, nor establish Ares.
may I not be a dear companion either in evils or in prosperity.

In Doric in lyric passages μάτηρ [mother] with genitive and dative ματρός ματρί [of a mother, to a mother], or where the meter demands ματέρος ματέρι [of a mother, to a mother], which forms are foreign to the dialogue parts, in which the use of the disyllabic form μητρός μητρί [of a mother, to a mother] is constant: but the accusative is everywhere trisyllabic μητέρα [mother], or in lyric passages ματέρα [mother]) mother.
